extracted.intended_audience: general readers and policymakers interested in foreign affairs and historical documents
extracted.subtask_description: AP news coverage summarizing the recently released Yalta conference papers, official reactions, political fallout, and related Cold War developments. Focused on documenting facts, quotations, and responses from U.S., British, German and other officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement-in-principle vs implemented policy
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In the end the three appeared to be in agreement on the principle of dismemberment; however, the agreement never came to fruition in actual policy applied to Germany.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between what leaders agreed to in principle at Yalta and what was actually implemented postwar; account for unplanned outcomes (e.g., East-West split) when judging the significance of wartime accords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for granting an occupation zone
rubrics_metrics.description: Questioning whether 'France should have a zone of occupation, and for what reason.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require a clear, defensible rationale for granting an occupying power its own zone (strategic, political, logistical); note objections from other parties and insist the reason be examined 'further' before committing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for direct military communication/cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Roosevelt hoped 'Gen. Dwight D. Eisenhower would shortly be able to communicate directly with the Soviet command.' Stalin thought that 'was very important.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate plans for coalition operations on criteria of directness and clarity of military communications and staff coordination; judge proposals by whether they provide workable channels for operational collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of atomic energy matters (secrecy and disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'No available records, however, contain any indication that atomic energy matters were discussed with the British at Malta or with either the British or the Russians at Yalta.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat atomic-energy discussions as exceptionally sensitive; expect restricted circulation and limited documentation. When assessing released records, note whether sensitive topics were kept out of conference records and whether that omission was deliberate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declassification, labeling and publication costs/security
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The first printing was labeled "TOP SECRET" ... Security of that sort runs up the cost. ... the second revision -- which is the one made public tonight -- was downgraded to "FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY." '
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of formerly classified records should follow formal declassification steps and account for security-driven costs and redactions; track label changes and their implications for what can be publicly released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and censorship of released papers
rubrics_metrics.description: McCarthy said he had been informed that '150 persons have had a hand in censoring the papers, so what you get will not be the full story.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess released document sets for completeness and potential censorship; identify how many and which offices reviewed/edited materials and consider that in evaluating authenticity and reliability of the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and diplomatic consequences of public release
rubrics_metrics.description: British officials said publication 'could help to discourage the Russians from joining in top-level talks' and that release 'was inadvisable' — critics called the U.S. decision 'a major blunder.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publishing sensitive historical records, weigh likely diplomatic repercussions and whether disclosure could harm ongoing negotiations or foreign-policy objectives; include consultation with affected governments when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to explain sensitive decisions to domestic audiences before disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Churchill said that bringing out an agreement 'now without any explanation of U.S. position will cause trouble.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive international agreements or concessions should be accompanied by clear explanations to domestic constituencies to avoid misinterpretation and political backlash when documents are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political accountability vs historical interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments such as McCarthy calling the agreements 'infamous' and others saying the papers provide 'interesting historical reading, but ... will do nothing to settle our present day problems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between judging wartime decisions for political accountability (e.g., repudiation) and valuing documents for historical understanding; consider whether publication serves current policy debates or primarily historical scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional/legal authority to transfer or 'Europeanize' territory
rubrics_metrics.description: The socialist suit would claim the Bonn government 'is not empowered to "sign away" German territory' and would argue it is 'illegal to deprive German citizens ... of their rights under the constitution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate international agreements altering territory against constitutional constraints: check whether domestic law permits the government to cede or change status of territory and whether citizens' constitutional rights are implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural threshold for constitutional challenge in West Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: A suit challenging government action 'can be filed on the demand of 1/3 of the Bundestag's 487 members.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing the legality/timeliness of political-constitutional actions, account for procedural requirements (e.g., fraction of parliament needed to trigger a court review) that affect litigation prospects and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export/embargo compliance for strategic goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials said a West Berlin company 'is charged with shipping war material to Red China' and that the company had 'pledged to observe the U.S. ban' on certain exports; customs caught shipments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies and officials should be judged by adherence to export controls and embargoes: evidence of prior violations, whether counterpart funds were used, and whether internal/external compliance checks were in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial/publishing tradeoffs: historical completeness vs security redaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Department prepared massive bound proofs 'which must still be corrected and sprinkled with nine ill—' and the publication involved heavy security editing and cost: 'The State Department spent more than the usual amount in preparing the Yalta papers because of the great length it went to in order to keep the vault.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and agencies must balance historical completeness against national-security redaction and cost; document the editorial process, note how many proofs and revisions were made, and disclose the rationale for redactions where possible.
